gap: No result ChatGPT got states that EcoFlow's US store lists the original DELTA Pro Ultra (ChatGPT's 'from $5,143' pick) as unavailable, while its in-stock successor, the DELTA Pro Ultra X, costs $7,899 for 12 kW and 12 kWh. Over the same 12–14 kWh range, the EG4 FlexBOSS21 plus a 14.3 kWh PowerPro costs $6,724.98 in hardware at Signature Solar (about $470/kWh), and Sun Gold Power's SPH6548P plus 10.24 kWh costs $2,988 (about $292/kWh).
standout_why: I compared three cited pages. EnergySage (dated 2026-05-11) gives only installed price per kWh, from quotes collected October 2025 to March 2026: Powerwall 3 $998/kWh, aPower 2 $1,177/kWh, EG4 WallMount $1,163/kWh. It has no hardware prices and no EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra. iTechGuides (2026-10-25) prices only EcoFlow, using Amazon listings ($4,199 for the DELTA Pro Ultra, $6,199 for a 12 kWh bundle). It does not price the EG4 setup or the DELTA Pro Ultra X. SolutionEnergy (2026-10-03) lists the DELTA Pro Ultra at $4,199, the Anker E10 at $3,999 and the Apex 300 at $1,499 as of October 2026. None of the three says the original DELTA Pro Ultra is unavailable from EcoFlow, or prices the X successor, the EG4 inverter-plus-battery pair, or a 48 V DIY kit. The Anker E10 starter kit has also gone from $3,999 to $4,299. The rivals do have Powerwall and FranklinWH per-kWh installed costs, so that part is not new.
decides: It changes ChatGPT's #3 pick. The DELTA Pro Ultra at 'from $5,143' is listed as unavailable on EcoFlow's US store; the buyable replacement costs $7,899. At that price it costs more than ChatGPT's 'best value' EG4 pair ($6,724.98 for 12 kW on battery and 14.3 kWh) while giving less storage. That confirms EG4 as the DIY value pick. For a buyer who wants a plug-in, no-electrician setup, the Anker SOLIX E10 with 2 batteries ($5,999 for 12.288 kWh, about $488/kWh) now undercuts EcoFlow. Tesla Powerwall 3 stays the only single-box integrated pick, but at about $998/kWh installed (EnergySage) it costs roughly twice as much per kWh as the DIY hardware.
